transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Avery Kim (Redwood CSM), Miguel Torres (AtlasPayments - Head of Security), Leah Wong (SRE), Samir Patel (Platform PM), Dana Rivera (IT Ops)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros, I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood. Priya is our solutions engineer and Avery on customer success. Miguel, want to kick us off with expectations for this security deep dive?

[00:18] Miguel Torres: Sure thanks. We're looking to validate SSO and SCIM flows, make sure we can do least-privilege RBAC for production teams, and confirm audit logging and encryption practices before we move to a pilot. Also data residency questions — payments data so we have requirements.

[00:35] Priya Shah: Great, we'll walk through our SSO/SAML setup first, then SCIM provisioning, then RBAC patterns, and finally logging/encryption and residency. Please interrupt with specifics.

[00:50] Leah Wong: Quick note — our identity provider is Okta, but we also have a few customers on Azure AD. We need to confirm attribute mappings and SCIM compatibility.

[01:05] Priya Shah: Okta/Azure AD supported, we have metadata exchange for SAML and a SCIM 2.0 connector. For SSO we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, and SAML assertions validate against audience and issuer.

[01:30] Samir Patel: How are SAML attributes mapped to roles? We want to enforce least-privilege — devs shouldn't get ops-level access.

[01:45] Priya Shah: We recommend mapping group attributes to Redwood roles. Example: SAML group claim groups contains: redwood-admins -> platform-admin role, redwood-devs -> workspace-developer role. SCIM will sync group membership and user attributes. You can also set up a default minimal role and then grant elevated roles only via SCIM group.

[02:10] Miguel Torres: If we do SCIM provisioning, can we have one-way sync from IdP and manage deprovision events automatically? Deprovision timing matters for compliance.

[02:25] Priya Shah: Yes, SCIM supports provisioning and deprovision. When a user is deactivated in IdP, the SCIM PATCH call updates the user status to inactive in Redwood. We honor deactivated status immediately and can also trigger session invalidation. There may be a small propagation window, typically under a minute in our hosted environment.

[02:50] Dana Rivera: Session invalidation — can you kill active tokens and revoke API keys when a user is deprovisioned? That's critical for us.

[03:05] Priya Shah: We support API key rotation and revocation. Deprovision can optionally trigger automatic revocation of web sessions and user-scoped API keys. For service-level API keys, you can store them in a separate service account that isn't tied to a user.

[03:30] Jordan Lee: One thing to call out — for customers on Redwood Private, you can tie KMS-managed keys to your HSM/KMS and keep control; for hosted customers we offer KMS-managed encryption with customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in supported regions.

[03:55] Miguel Torres: Can you explain how encryption at rest works? Payment data must be encrypted with customer-managed keys if possible.

[04:10] Priya Shah: Sure. At rest, data is encrypted using AES-256. For hosted, we support CMKs via AWS KMS — you provide the KMS key ARN and we encrypt data at rest with envelope encryption using that CMK. On Private, keys never leave your control and we can integrate with on-prem HSMs.

[04:35] Leah Wong: What about audit logs — what's captured, retention, and export options?

[04:50] Priya Shah: Audit logs capture authentication events (SAML asserts, successful/failed logins), admin changes (role grants, SCIM changes), model/inference calls metadata (not the full PII/text payload by default — we can configure). Retention default is 90 days for hosted, with retention add-ons for longer. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM via S3 export, CloudWatch, or syslog connectors in Private setups.

[05:20] Miguel Torres: We need immutable logs for 365 days. Is that supported? And chain of custody?

[05:30] Jordan Lee: Yes, for enterprise customers we offer extended retention add-ons. For hosted, we can export rolling snapshots to your S3 bucket and enable object lock for immutability. For Private deployments, logs stay in your environment and follow your retention policies. We can provide log signing or ingestion to custody tracking tools if required.

[05:55] Samir Patel: Back to RBAC, can we create custom roles scoped to a model or workspace? Our dev teams need access to sandbox models but not prod models.

[06:10] Priya Shah: Absolutely. Roles are namespace-scoped. We support org-level and workspace-level roles. You can define custom roles — each role is a set of permissions (read/write/invoke/manage models, billing view, admin). Example: sandbox-invoke-only role which can call models in sandbox workspaces but cannot deploy or change configs in prod.

[06:40] Leah Wong: How is least-privilege enforced operationally? Do you have an audit of role changes and can we require two-person approval for elevated privileges?

[06:55] Priya Shah: Role changes are audited. We also support approval workflows via integration with your ticketing system (we can require an approval step before role grants for enterprise setups). For stricter controls, customers often put privileged operations behind a separate admin team or require SCIM group-based grants that only admins can set.

[07:20] Miguel Torres: Are there any default privileged accounts we should be aware of? And can we disable any out-of-band admin access?

[07:35] Jordan Lee: By default the initial org owner has super-admin privileges; you can rotate and limit that account. For Redwood-managed support, we only access tenant data with explicit consent via support sessions and all support actions are logged and require an approval ticket for sensitive operations. You can also request support access be disabled entirely for Private deployments.

[07:55] Dana Rivera: Network side — for VPC/private mode, do you support private endpoints and restrict egress? We need to ensure no traffic leaves our VPC except to necessary services.

[08:10] Priya Shah: Yes, Private supports VPC peering, private endpoints, and egress filters. We'll review your network diagram in the VPC review session. For hosted, we can restrict data plane regions and support private peering in some cloud providers.

[08:35] Miguel Torres: A couple of compliance Qs: SOC 2 and ISO27001 — do you have current reports? And how often are they refreshed?

[08:50] Jordan Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs; they are updated annually. Jordan (AE) will share the latest reports and the compliance pack after this call. For customers with NDA we can provide the full attestations and SOC 3 summary publicly.

[09:10] Miguel Torres: Good. Also interested in encryption in transit — mutual TLS?

[09:20] Priya Shah: All API traffic uses TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites. For Private we support mTLS for internal service-to-service communication and can enable client cert validation for control plane access.

[09:40] Samir Patel: SCIM specifics — what attributes do you accept? We have custom attributes like employeeNumber and costCenter that we'd like to map to tags/labels.

[09:55] Priya Shah: SCIM 2.0 schema supports custom attributes; we also accept core attributes like userName, name, emails, active, groups. We can map custom attributes to user metadata fields that are available in RBAC policies and for billing tags. We'll share example SCIM payloads.

[10:15] Leah Wong: Error handling — if SCIM provisioning fails for a user, how is that surfaced? Retries?

[10:25] Priya Shah: Failures are logged and surfaced via admin UI with a retry queue. We also send webhooks for provisioning failures so your IdP can alert and we maintain a backlog for manual reconciliation.

[10:40] Miguel Torres: How do you handle service accounts vs human users? We want to ensure service accounts can't be used to escalate privileges.

[10:50] Priya Shah: We recommend service accounts be created as dedicated service principals with limited scopes and no interactive session tokens. Service accounts should be tied to org-level service roles and their keys should be rotated regularly. We can enforce policy where service accounts cannot be granted admin-level perms unless via a separate process.

[11:15] Jordan Lee: On detection/response — we surface suspicious activity: anomalous token use, large data egress, repeated failed auth. Those integrate with your SIEM and can trigger automated lockouts if needed.

[11:35] Leah Wong: Is there built-in SOC alerts mapping to MITRE or similar?

[11:45] Priya Shah: We provide event types and mappings; for advanced correlation customers usually ingest alerts to their SIEM where they map to MITRE and set up playbooks.
transcript_continued:
[12:00] Miguel Torres: On retention again, can we set different retention for audit logs versus model request metadata? We don't want to store raw model inputs longer than necessary.

[12:15] Priya Shah: Yes, by default request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts, requestor) is kept longer than payload. Raw request bodies (if you opt into debug logging) are stored separately and can be configured to purge after X days. We also have an option to not store payloads at all — stream-only mode where responses are ephemeral and logs only contain metadata.

[12:40] Samir Patel: For pilot, we'd like a setup where debug logs are off and minimal metadata retained. How easy is it to switch once we're in pilot to enabling more detailed logs for troubleshooting?

[12:55] Priya Shah: It's a config toggle in environment settings; enabling debug requires an approval step for hosted production tenants due to sensitivity. For pilot orgs it's straightforward to flip on and off.

[13:15] Dana Rivera: About SAML metadata exchange — do you support metadata URL or file upload?

[13:25] Priya Shah: Both. You can upload IdP metadata XML or provide an auto-refreshing metadata URL. We recommend the metadata URL for rotation.

[13:40] Miguel Torres: What about SCIM rate limits? We have a large org and bulk provisioning will happen.

[13:50] Priya Shah: We have tiered rate limits. For enterprise customers we provide a higher rate limit or a one-time bulk provisioning endpoint for initial syncs. Ongoing syncs are incremental. We'll include recommended pagination and retry semantics in the SCIM docs.

[14:10] Jordan Lee: Also worth mentioning that role changes via SCIM are auditable and appear in the admin audit trail with before/after state.

[14:25] Leah Wong: Can we configure session timeout and MFA enforcement?

[14:35] Priya Shah: Yes. Session timeout policies can be org-level and you can require SSO-enforced MFA. We honor the IdP's MFA policies; for additional security you can require step-up authentication for certain operations.

[14:55] Miguel Torres: For policy compliance we may need periodic attestation that certain users still have privileged roles. Any support for certification workflows?

[15:05] Priya Shah: We support role certification workflows via integrations with your IAM/cert tooling; otherwise we can export role membership snapshots to S3 for your attestation process.

[15:25] Samir Patel: Can you show a quick walkthrough of the admin UI for role mapping? (screen sharing)

[15:35] Jordan Lee: We'll do a short demo. Priya, can you pull up the admin console?

[15:45] [screen share starts]
[16:00] Priya Shah: Here is org settings -> SSO -> SAML config. You can upload metadata, define assertion consumer service URL, configure attribute mappings. Under provisioning we enter the SCIM base URL and bearer token.

[16:25] Miguel Torres: Where do we map groups to roles?

[16:30] Priya Shah: Under Access Management -> Role mappings. You can create a mapping: SAML group claim "payments-admins" -> Redwood role "org-admin". You can also add conditions based on attributes like costCenter.

[16:50] Leah Wong: Are role mappings tested with a dry-run? We want to validate before applying to real users.

[16:58] Priya Shah: There's a test user feature that simulates SAML assertion and shows which roles would be granted. SCIM preview shows delta before apply for bulk ops.

[17:15] Dana Rivera: If we need to enforce separation of duties, can we prevent one person from having both infra-deploy and billing roles?

[17:25] Priya Shah: Currently we provide role constraints policies where you can set mutually exclusive role sets. That's available for enterprise customers and we can enable it for AtlasPayments pilot.

[17:50] Samir Patel: Regarding support access earlier, can you detail the approval process if we request Redwood support to access our tenant for troubleshooting?

[17:58] Jordan Lee: Support access is by default disabled; when needed we create a time-limited session, require a JIRA/ticket approval, and every action is logged. We can also provide transcripts of support sessions on request.

[18:15] Miguel Torres: Good. On legal side, do you have DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses for EU data?

[18:25] Jordan Lee: Yes we have a DPA and SCCs. For EU-hosted data we support region-specific hosting. We'll attach the DPA to the compliance pack.

[18:40] Leah Wong: For data residency, if we choose a US-only region, will any metadata or logs be replicated outside US for analytics?

[18:50] Priya Shah: No — for region-restricted customers we isolate data plane and logs to the specified region. Some global control plane metadata may be stored in our control plane, but sensitive customer data remains in the chosen region. We'll provide a detailed data flow diagram in the VPC review.

[19:10] Miguel Torres: Can you confirm backups and snapshots are encrypted and controlled?

[19:20] Priya Shah: Backups are encrypted with the same CMK and we can configure key rotation policies. Snapshots destined for S3 are encrypted server-side; for extra custody you can require client-side encryption to your S3 bucket.

[19:40] Samir Patel: Any customer-facing telemetry or error reporting that may leak sensitive data?

[19:50] Priya Shah: We redacted PII in telemetry by default. Customers can opt into deeper telemetry for debugging but it's gated. Also, debug sessions are auditable.

[20:05] Miguel Torres: Let's talk about lifecycle: if we terminate the contract, how is data deletion handled?

[20:15] Jordan Lee: We have a documented offboarding process: we can securely wipe data, provide a data export in a mutually agreed format, and validate deletion with certificate. Retention and deletion terms are in the DPA. For Private deployments data remains on your infra so you control deletion.

[20:35] Leah Wong: Any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?

[20:45] Jordan Lee: We maintain a subprocessors list in the compliance pack. Typical ones are cloud provider, monitoring vendor, and analytics platform — all vetted. We can provide subprocessors and their regions.

[21:00] Miguel Torres: For our pilot we want minimal privilege, payload redaction, and 90-day logs with export to our SIEM. Does Redwood support that config?

[21:12] Priya Shah: Yes, that's a common enterprise pilot config. We can set default role minimal, SCIM-provision groups control, disable debug payload storage, set 90-day audit retention and scheduled exports to your S3/SIEM.

[21:30] Samir Patel: About scaling: if during pilot we hit throughput spikes, do you auto-scale and how does that affect audit/e2e observability?

[21:45] Priya Shah: Hosted auto-scaling is transparent; logs remain consistent and are tagged with instance IDs. For Dedicated we size GPU pools; scaling events are tracked in the audit logs.

[22:05] Miguel Torres: Any known gaps we should plan for?

[22:12] Jordan Lee: For most customers everything maps, but specific enterprise features like two-person approval and mutually exclusive role enforcement need to be enabled per account. We'll outline gaps in the compliance pack and implementation plan.

[22:30] Dana Rivera: Can you provide a sample network diagram and recommended security groups for VPC peering?

[22:45] Priya Shah: Yes we'll include a sample network diagram and firewall/security group recommendations in the VPC review packet.

[23:00] Miguel Torres: Ok let's surface a few risk items: SCIM failures could lead to orphaned accounts, log export failures could delay incident response. How do you recommend we mitigate?

[23:15] Priya Shah: Mitigate with monitoring and alerts on provisioning failures, daily reconciliation jobs, and S3 export health checks. We'll provide runbooks and playbooks.

[23:35] Samir Patel: One operational question — who owns the SCIM bearer token and how often should it rotate?

[23:45] Priya Shah: You can generate the SCIM bearer token in Redwood and store it in your IdP. Rotate regularly— recommended every 90 days. For extra security use an ephemeral token via a middle broker if you have that capability.

[24:00] Jordan Lee: We're approaching the demo portion end. Any remaining must-have requirements that would block pilot?

[24:10] Miguel Torres: Must-haves: SSO w/ Okta, SCIM deprovision immediate, session kill on deprovision, audit exports to our SIEM, CMK support for encryption at rest, regional hosting in US only. If those are met we're good to pilot.

[24:35] Jordan Lee: That's fair. We'll commit to that pilot configuration. We'll send the compliance docs and an implementation plan.

[24:50] Leah Wong: Two more clarifying points: how do you handle model telemetry which may include user prompts? We need to ensure prompts are not retained by default.

[25:05] Priya Shah: By default model inputs are persisted only as metadata; prompt retention is opt-in for debugging. We'll default pilot to not store prompts and can provision a debug pipeline with strict controls if you need debug sessions.

[25:30] Samir Patel: For the billing view, can we restrict access to finance team only?

[25:38] Priya Shah: Yes billing roles are separate and you can scope billing visibility to specific groups.

[25:50] Miguel Torres: Ok let's confirm next steps and owners.

[26:00] Jordan Lee: Action items: I'll send the compliance pack and SOC/ISO certs; Priya will share SSO/SCIM docs and SCIM sample payloads; Avery will provision a trial org and invite your SREs; Leah please share your IdP metadata and attribute mappings. We'll schedule a VPC/network review for next week.

[26:25] Miguel Torres: Sounds good. Any questions from Redwood side?

[26:30] Leah Wong: Nothing else.

[26:35] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll follow up via email with the links. Thanks everyone.

[26:45] [call ends — informal chatter and wrap up]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" pronounced "K-V cash" earlier in diagrams; proper nouns like some product names spelled inconsistently. This transcript is auto-generated and lightly edited for readability.
